key_insight: Detonation-spray settings strongly control whether self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings become denser and harder or more wear-resistant, with clear trade-offs between friction and durability.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical parameter guidance for restoring and strengthening machine parts using detonation-sprayed nickel-based coatings.
method: Varied barrel filling level from 48–68% to tune coating density and defect formation.
Adjusted gas molar ratio (O/C = 1.026–1.856) and inter-shot delay (0–1 s) to influence microstructure and tribology.
Evaluated coatings using morphology, roughness, hardness, friction, and specific wear rate tests.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a minimum friction coefficient of 0.674 ± 0.136 at 48% filling and O/C = 1.026, while the best wear resistance reached a specific wear rate of 0.000189 mm³/(N·m) at O/C = 1.856 with 1 s inter-shot delay.
watch_item: Optimizing for low friction can increase wear, so process settings must be balanced for the intended service condition rather than tuned to a single metric.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
